description: Find the longest induced (chord-free) open path in the n-dimensional hypercube. A classic combinatorial search problem with a published record table (proven optimal through n=7, best-known lower bounds beyond); used in error-correcting code design. Verification is an exact re-check of the returned vertex sequence.

problem_shape.objective: maximize snake length (edges) of an induced path in Q_n under a fixed candidate-extension evaluation budget
problem_shape.input_representation: hypercube dimension n (vertices are integers 0..2^n-1; adjacency = Hamming distance 1), a seed, and an evaluation budget
problem_shape.output_representation: a sequence of vertex integers forming the snake, starting from the canonical edge 0 -> 1
constraints: consecutive vertices differ in exactly one bit
no two non-consecutive vertices are adjacent (chord-free / skin condition)
all vertices distinct and in range [0, 2^n)
search must respect the evaluation budget passed to solve()
failure_modes: returning a path with a chord (validator rejects; NaN poisons the score)
counting vertices instead of edges (length = edges = len(seq)-1)
ignoring the budget and brute-forcing (unfair vs baselines at equal budget)
hardcoding a known snake from the literature instead of searching (holdout uses unseen seeds; identical outputs across seeds are suspicious)

recommended_problem_template: Develop a novel search method for the snake-in-the-box problem (longest induced path in the hypercube Q_n) that beats restarted stochastic beam search at an equal evaluation budget on dimensions 6-8.
compose_query_hints: nested rollout policy adaptation combinatorial search
Monte Carlo tree search combinatorial optimization
